recipe.notes:
One family, three sizes (decision 34), the evidence for one: the pipeline files agree byte for byte (modules.json, config_sentence_transformers.json, mteb_v2_eval_prompts.json identical at all three pinned revisions; 1_Pooling/config.json differs only in word_embedding_dimension), the cards are the same text with the same usage for all three sizes, and the served path is identical: --runner pooling, convert auto -> embed, the pooler from the checkpoints' own sentence-transformers metadata (last-token + L2 normalize), causal attention, bfloat16, no plugin, no trust-remote-code, no template file. The backbones differ (Gemma3TextModel 270m/27b, Qwen3Model 0.6b) and each variant's tokenizer follows from its model id (injected per variant); the only template-visible consequence is which post-processor token the route appends (the anchor declaration covers both), and the dims 640/1024/5376 are the checkpoints' own (no Matryoshka field exists in the cards, so the client declares none). Served = the client renders the template (the query prompt for queries, bare text for documents) and POSTs strings to /v1/embeddings; vLLM v0.31.0 serves each checkpoint with --runner pooling only. Prompt format: the frame ends "Query: " WITH a trailing space -- the checkpoint's own web_search_query prompt carries it (config_sentence_transformers.json, byte-pinned) and the card's get_detailed_instruct f-string writes "Query: {query}" the same way; the other preconfigured prompts (sts_query, bitext_query) are other tasks' frames -- specialising the task means a new recipe whose frame is that prompt (a new content identity), never a per-run field. Instructions (decision 33): the checkpoint's mteb_v2_eval_prompts.json holds the model's 131 per-task instructions; decision 33 assigns them to Dataset.task_instruction (model-owned, per task) and this family's target placement is the card's own fold: "Instruct: <instruction>\nQuery: <text>" -- this recipe's frame is exactly that fold with the retrieval default baked in, so a task-specialised recipe replaces the Instruct text and keeps the frame (the card's own usage wins over the generic Task: prefix, decision 9). The field's product-side plumbing ships with the embed role's title and instruction handling (the data-layer work behind those fields), so a task-specialised serving recipe is a new content identity. A per-query instruction (Query.instruction) no template slot exists for on the embed roles: the generic appended default applies product-side when a dataset carries one, and any instruction a pairs row carries is ignored on both sides of the equivalence check. Anchor: the served route appends the tokenizer's post-processor token and last-token pooling reads it -- both shapes end on their content span and pin add_special_tokens: true (the Gemma variants append the eos token, id 1, and lead with bos id 2; the 0.6b's Qwen tokenizer appends the endoftext id 151643 -- measured at the pinned revisions). The card's example (its own queries and documents) renders to 27 framed-query ids per variant and ends on the anchor (measured, pinned by the family test). Budgets: client.max_tokens is 32768 -- the card's "Max Tokens" for every variant and the transformers snippet's max_length; the cut applies to the content spans only, after reserving the frame (19-20 content ids of head, measured) and the appended anchor, and re-attaching the frame, so the anchor always survives. The card's transformers path truncates ids at 32768 (tokenizer(truncation=True, max_length=32768)); its sentence-transformers path truncates at the Transformer module's max_seq_length, which sentence-transformers infers when the checkpoint sets none (no sentence_bert_config.json, no max_seq_length in modules.json) as min(config.max_position_embeddings, tokenizer.model_max_length) (models/Transformer.py at >=3.0) -- 32768 for the 270m and the 0.6b, 131072 for the 27b -- and the post-processor appends the anchor after truncation, so it survives that cut too (measured at the pinned revisions); the client cuts verbatim text: over the cap the content boundary can differ while both keep the anchor, so the recipe declares over_cap_cut_differs, the reference's render is the card's own prompt (it never ports the client's cut), over-cap rows ride the harness's non-gating table and under-cap rows gate byte-exactly. No separate query cap exists in the referent -- the card truncates queries and documents alike at 32768 -- so query_max_tokens is not declared and both shapes draw on max_tokens. Wiring: every request is fitted to the declared budget on the wire by the merged product's embedding client (rcp_ndcg.data.preprocess.fit), audited in stage 1 against the captured wire. The 27b's 131072 max_position_embeddings is NOT served: the card declares Max Tokens 32,768 for every variant (its transformers snippet truncates at 32768), and serving the full context would put the GPU-E1 32-bit element-index limits under one forward of 131072 tokens -- the MLP activation alone is 131072 x 21504 (intermediate_size) = 2.82e9 elements, over 2^31 (2,147,483,648), the fault class that killed pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview at 262144 (GPU-E1); at the card's own 32768 the same product is 32768 x 21504 = 7.0e8 elements, well under. Pooling hang: on v0.31.0 a pooling prompt of exactly max_model_len tokens can stick under the default chunked prefill (max_num_batched_tokens 16384 on the >=160 GB GPUs; GPU-E1; fixed upstream in vllm#48039). ALL THREE VARIANTS NEED THE OPT-IN: client.max_tokens == serve.max_model_len == 32768, so the client's over-cap cut lands exactly on the documented trigger, and no flag workaround ships (a --max-num-batched-tokens raise would re-open the 32-bit arithmetic the 27b's budget exists to avoid, and the flag is not the recipe's contract). The family declares `serve.patches: [pooling-full-context]`, so the serve path exports the opt-in and the engine applies the upstream fix; the wave monitors the at-budget ladder. The engine image's transformers pin at the tag is >=5.10.4,<5.18.0 (requirements/common.txt); the tokenizer files are pinned by revision and the stage-1 zero-tolerance token-id check on the GPU host is the designed catch for library drift. No media processor settings apply: the models are text-only (input: [text], no processor files in any of the three repos). resources.gpus: 1 for every variant: the 27b's bf16 weights are ~54 GB, inside one B200. Reference environment: requirements-reference.txt (sentence-transformers for the card's usage; render mode needs only huggingface-hub -- see reference.py).


The 270m size: a Gemma3TextModel backbone (config.json model_type gemma3_text, 18 layers, hidden 640, intermediate 2048) whose layer_types are all full_attention -- the config's sliding_window 512 and sliding_window_pattern 1 never apply (vLLM reads layer_types per layer, gemma3.py:153-156), so every layer is global causal attention. Embedding dim 640 (1_Pooling/config.json word_embedding_dimension). The tokenizer appends the eos token (id 1) after the content and leads with bos (id 2) -- the appended eos is the pooled anchor.
